title: §.XIII close: Not tearing AC — human writing ≠ God's word; Calvin subscribed; fax furiae Gallicae restored
pass_a_gloss: For it is one thing to tear the Augsburg Confession with insults, or in any way to lessen its due Authority (which was never marked out by any of the Reformers), another to be unwilling to permit that a human Writing, and therefore liable to error, should come into the same census with the infallible word of God. Crocius examines the whole matter professedly in Comment. cap. 36 from p. 497. Calvin's Judgment concerning the Augsburg Confession — to be subscribed by him promptly at other times, nay subscribed in the very act (as he testifies in his Letter to Martin Schalingius, Pastor of Regensburg, in the Year 1557, in the Volume of Letters not so long ago edited at Amsterdam with all the Works, p. m. 112.) — when he somewhere calls the Augsburg Confession a torch of Gallic fury, read restored to its genuine sense, both in Pareus Fren. p. 294, and in the Author of the ausführlichen Behauptung p. 74 and following, and most fully of all in Joh. Crocius, Comment. often cited, pp. 514, 515, 518.
pass_b_english: For it is one thing to tear the Augsburg Confession with insults, or somehow to lower its due authority — which no Reformer ever set out to do — and another to refuse to let a human writing, liable to error, stand in the same rank as God's infallible word.
Crocius works the whole question through in Comm. cap. 36 from p. 497.

As for Calvin's judgment on the Augsburg Confession: he was ready to subscribe it at other times, and in fact did subscribe it (see his 1557 letter to Martin Schalingius, pastor at Regensburg, in the Letters volume lately edited at Amsterdam with the Opera, p. 112).

When elsewhere he calls the Augsburg Confession a torch of Gallic fury, read that restored to its genuine sense — in Pareus (Fren. p. 294), in the Ausführliche Behauptung (p. 74ff.), and most fully in Crocius (Comm. pp. 514, 515, 518).
source_text: Nam aliud est, August. Confess. convitiis proscindere, vel quoquô modô debitam illius Auctoritatem elevare (quod à Reformatorum nemine unquam designatum est) aliud, non permittere velle, quòd humanum Scriptum, eóque errori obnoxium, cum infallibili Dei verbo, in eundem censum veniat. Rem omnem ex professo excutit Crocius Comment. cap. 36. a p. 497. Calvini Judicium de Augustana Confessione, ab eo promptè aliàs subscribenda, imò actu ipso subscripta (uti testatur in Epistola sua ad Martinum Schalingium Pastorem Ratisbonensem Anno 1557., Epistolarum Tomô, non ita pridem cum Operibus omnibus Amstelodami editô, p. m. 112.), quando Aug. Confessionem facem furiae Gallicae alicubi appellitat, genuino suo sensui restitutum lege, tùm apud Pareum Fren. p. 294, tùm apud Auctorem der ausführlichen Behauptung p. 74. & seqq. omniumq; plenissimè apud Joh. Crocium, Comment. saepius citat. p. 514. 515. 518.
